- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, cap the next 3–5 periods at 10–15% below peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.4) and forecast is below recent history, adjust upward by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day trend.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and forecast is consistently 5–8% above true outcome, apply downward bias correction by 2–3% per period.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to allow market momentum to settle.
